catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-16 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. Blind reading.
Beyond the rules: I listed the packet directory and read image pixel sizes (sips) to see which images are overviews and which are tiles. Nothing else.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of face A)
- Orientation: upright. Fragment assembled from two (possibly three) parchment strips mounted with clear tape on a dark background, ruler (cm, 0-17) below.
- An L/T-shaped assembly: an upright piece at top right (approx. 8.5 cm wide) carrying ~19 lines of a single column, with a red/brown "iii"-like mark (probably a quire/leaf signature or running number) in the upper margin; its right edge is torn with losses at lines 3-8.
- Below/left: a horizontal strip ~ 21 cm wide carrying two blocks of text side by side: left block ~13 lines (lower part of a column, with blank lower margin beneath), right block ~13 lines continuing under the upright piece. Interpretation (tentative): two columns of a two-column page, the upright piece being the upper part of the right column (col. b) and the horizontal strip the lower part of both columns; text of col. b seems to run on from the upright piece into the strip ("...ut celebrat" / "sit ..."). Not certain the upper piece joins directly.
- Left block has a red rubric inline at line 3: "De sententia exco..." (red ink). Some words underlined (red/brown strokes) e.g. "ad absolvendum", "evidenter".
- A catchword/word in lower margin under left column: "Itetio"? (to check).
- Script: small Gothic textualis, heavily abbreviated; prose with what look like (tentative interpretation) legal allegations ("ibi dicit", "ex. de ...").
- Two holes in the horizontal strip (worm or sewing).

- Face B: see image-005 survey below.
Selected spans: all legible lines on every tile (the fragment is small, so I attempt full transcription of what survives). Torn right edge of the upright piece (lines 3-8 of image-002) and line ends lost there remain unread.

ABBREVIATION CONVENTIONS used below: (x) = proposed expansion of an abbreviation; word? = uncertain reading; [illegible] = unreadable; [...] = lost to tear/edge. "p(er)/p(ro)/p(re)" from the usual p-signs; "q(uod)" for the q with stroke; "(et)" for tironian et; "(con)" for the 9-shaped sign.
